findingDetails.title: The Vibe row ignores the hook match filter, so an entry Vibe never runs on a main turn still reads ok vibe
findingDetails.claim: tomlCommands captures only type and command, and inspect accepts any pre_agent block whose command ends with the marker, so a match value other than main still reads ok.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the real hooks file and the repository uses match on this event family, including agents_spawn, while the check never reads the key.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The check could be read as entry-presence only; even then a filtered entry is not the prompt entry it claims to report.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: None; a target-repository block with another match value is a concrete false pass.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The check and its test are declared scope files; the hooks file and README are the code and claim it must match.

findingDetails.title: The hook contract names Vibe in its per-runtime table but leaves it out of the two runtime summaries that table feeds
findingDetails.claim: The section intro and the starting-a-surfaced-command table omit Vibe while the new Vibe row says it uses the shared handler and needs the document line.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the Vibe row and the handler path; the row describes the shared handler and the document line, so the summaries are stale rather than describing a different design.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Vibe could be excluded from the table because it has no command loader; the table already has a no row for every other runtime without a loader, so the exclusion is inconsistent.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: None; the doc addition is the changed line set.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The hook contract is a declared scope file and the Vibe row is the changed line; the code it describes is in scope.
